summary: Tested backlog: WhatsApp Medication Reminders (auto-schedule from prescription frequency/duration) + Consultations pagination. Backend: 13/14 pass (93%). All parser, auto-schedule, CRUD, recep permission, regression (empty-frequency Rx 200), consultations pagination shape & clamp tests pass. ONE backend bug found: past-end-date reminders are NOT auto-marked 'completed' by send_due_medication_reminders() — they are silently skipped by an outer `continue` before the completion branch in `_process_one` is reached. Twilio absent → send_whatsapp_message returns None gracefully (no exception), but because the send fails, sent_log is never appended, so dedup is effectively trivial in this env (cannot be exercised end-to-end without Twilio creds). Frontend: /reminders renders MedicationRemindersPanel below Appointment/Follow-up/Feedback cards, 10 auto-created reminders displayed, pause→resume toggle works, delete buttons present. /consultations renders without crash with paginated response.

minor.issue: Past-end-date reminders are NOT auto-marked status='completed'. The outer loop in `send_due_medication_reminders` does `if today > (rem.get('end_date') or today): continue` which short-circuits BEFORE reaching the dead-code completion branch in `_process_one`. Result: expired reminders linger as 'active' forever. Fix: replace the outer `continue` with an inline `await db.medication_reminders.update_one({'id': rem['id']}, {'$set': {'status':'completed'}})` then continue.

When Twilio is unconfigured (current env), send_whatsapp_message returns None, _process_one returns False, and sent_log is NEVER appended. So the 'idempotency via sent_log' guarantee only kicks in when sends succeed. If Twilio is intermittent, the same dose could resend on next 5-min tick. Consider appending sent_log even on a 'mock'/no-creds path or guarding with a separate 'attempted_log' for ops visibility.

rca of the issue: send_due_medication_reminders() main loop does `if today > (rem.get('end_date') or today): continue` BEFORE the inner times loop. This means an expired reminder is skipped entirely and never reaches _process_one(), where the `if reminder.get('end_date') and today > reminder['end_date']: $set status=completed` block exists. That branch is therefore dead code. Reproduction: insert a reminder with end_date=yesterday status='active', call send_due_medication_reminders(), observe status remains 'active'. Mitigation: in the outer loop, replace `continue` with `await db.medication_reminders.update_one({'id': rem['id']}, {'$set': {'status': 'completed'}})` then `continue`.
